comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C19-C21 regarding AGES system validation showing GFP expression levels and comparison with Gal80ts. Both evaluations find these technical validation results supported by the data.
Perfect agreement on claims C15, C22-C23 regarding delayed pupariation and strain-specific developmental effects. Both evaluations support these findings with no challenges noted.

Both address dose-response and survival claims C24-C29. OpenEval notes C28 is speculative about AGES resistance mechanism. Peer reviewers provide strong affirmation of auxin effects on survival rates with well-designed experiments.

Both address feeding behavior claims C30-C36. OpenEval finds FLIC data well-supported with C36 being inferential but reasonable. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm strong evidence for feeding activity alterations.

Both address metabolomics claims C37-C41. OpenEval finds sex-specific metabolic responses clearly demonstrated with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers explicitly support metabolomics findings using UHPLC-MS with appropriate quantification.

Both address TAG measurement claims C42-C46. OpenEval supports findings with sex:diet interaction data. Peer reviewers affirm significantly lower triglyceride levels in auxin-fed flies with solid results.

Both address TAG recovery claims C47-C52. OpenEval finds sex-specific reversibility demonstrated though C48 somewhat inferential. Peer reviewers support lipid metabolism findings as part of broader metabolomics validation.

OpenEval addresses summary claims C50, C61 integrating multiple data types. Peer R3 includes C50 in broader lipid metabolism support. Both find metabolic conclusions reasonably inferred from combined data.
OpenEval addresses C61 as summary conclusion from combined data. Peer R4 includes C61 in transcriptomic findings context. Both support integration of metabolic and transcriptomic evidence.

Both address xenobiotic response claims C53-C55. OpenEval finds RNA-seq and qRT-PCR validation support detoxification enzyme interpretation. Peer reviewers affirm transcriptome changes in fatty acid metabolism genes.

Both address paradoxical gene expression claims C56-C58. OpenEval finds pattern clearly demonstrated though biological interpretation uncertain. Peer reviewers affirm transcriptomic findings without challenging the paradoxical observations.

Both address mechanistic speculation claims C59-C60. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly speculative hypotheses not directly tested. Peer reviewers accept these as possibilities presented by authors without challenge.

Both address egg laying and hatching claims C73-C76. OpenEval finds data support conclusion that oocyte quality is unaffected. Peer reviewers explicitly support that fecundity does not seem affected using current assays.

Both address comprehensive oogenesis claims C77-C81. OpenEval finds conclusion that AGES doesn't affect oogenesis well-supported despite metabolic changes. Peer reviewers explicitly state female oogenesis does not seem affected.

Both address oogenesis integration claims C82-C84. OpenEval finds conclusions reasonable with appropriate qualification about suitability for 'some' processes. Peer reviewers conclude auxin could be appropriate for other biological processes.

Both address cautionary recommendations C88-C90. OpenEval finds recommendation to avoid AGES for lipid metabolism appropriately supported by persistent TAG changes. Peer reviewers strongly emphasize these cautions, noting researchers need awareness for experimental design.

Both address experimental design recommendations C91-C92, C94. OpenEval finds these reasonable based on findings and best practices. Peer reviewers emphasize researchers need to be careful when applying this strategy.

Both address background claims C1-C5 on Drosophila genetics methodologies. OpenEval finds these well-established with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accept contextual background without challenge.

Both address background claims C6-C8 on adverse effects of existing systems. OpenEval finds these well-supported by literature establishing rationale for AGES. Peer reviewers accept motivation for comparing auxin to other systems.

Both address AGES system description claims C9-C12. OpenEval finds appropriate literature citations with uncertainty about auxin effects motivating the study. Peer reviewers accept background on auxin-inducible systems as complement to Gal80ts.

Both address plant auxin background claims C62-C65. OpenEval finds these accurately describe established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers do not challenge these contextual statements about auxin in plants.

Both address comparative inference claims C66-C67. OpenEval finds C66 reasonable inference from TAG differences between Drosophila and plants, C67 appropriate recommendation. Peer reviewers accept contextual comparison without challenge.

Both address background claims C85-C87 on limitations of existing systems. OpenEval finds these supported by appropriate citations providing context for AGES evaluation. Peer reviewers accept this background establishing study motivation.
OpenEval addresses C93 as recommendation citing Hawley et al., 2023. Peer R8 includes C93 in accepted background claims. Both support this as appropriate guidance for experimental design.
OpenEval R1 addresses only background C1-C5, while Peer R1 addresses experimental findings C13-C14, C24-C36. No direct overlap except both evaluations are positive about their respective claim sets.

Peer reviewers address claims C13-C14 (study objectives and auxin effects overview) which are not explicitly grouped in any OpenEval result, though these themes are distributed across multiple OpenEval evaluations.

Peer reviewers address claim C16 (sex-specific metabolic responses overview) which appears in Peer R3 but is not explicitly grouped in OpenEval results, though the concept is covered across OpenEval R8-R10.
Peer reviewers address claim C18 (oogenesis investigation overview) which is included in Peer R5 but not explicitly in OpenEval results, though the findings are covered in OpenEval R17-R19.
Peer reviewers address claims C68-C72 (additional background on auxin biology and experimental considerations) which are included in Peer R8 but not explicitly evaluated in OpenEval results.
